title: Rerank throughput collapse during quantized model rollout — eviction thrash and kernel mismatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 we observed a ~60% drop in successful rerank inference throughput and large latency spikes (p50 from 45ms -> 210ms, p95 > 1.2s) across hosted regions following a controlled rollout of a new 4-bit quantized rerank model variant. The cascade was caused by interaction between the new quantized kernel selection path and the vectorstore eviction policy: the quantized path increased per-request KV-cache pressure and temporary GPU memory fragmentation, triggering aggressive shard eviction which led to repeated cold-loads and autoscaler oscillation. Several customer-facing queries failed or timed out until mitigations were applied. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-up work.

root_cause: Multiple interacting factors: (1) A new 4-bit quantized kernel path introduced changes to memory allocation patterns that increase short-lived GPU allocations for KV cache entries. (2) The vectorstore eviction policy used a tight free-memory threshold which considered these transient allocations as persistent pressure and evicted hot shards more aggressively than needed. (3) The autoscaler used a CPU-based metric that reacted to reduced in-flight requests rather than GPU memory pressure, causing scale-downs during the eviction recovery window and creating oscillation. (4) The canary automation increased traffic during the incident window and amplified effects because automated rollout continuation lacked a latency-safety interlock. Each factor alone would not cause the outage, but together they produced a positive feedback loop that collapsed throughput.
mitigations:
Immediate actions taken during incident: rollback rerank-v2-q4 canary to rerank-v1-fp16; temporarily increased autoscaler min-replicas in us-east-1 to prevent rapid scale-down; raised KV-cache eviction threshold to avoid evicting shards during transient allocation spikes; added guard to the rollout pipeline to pause if p95 latency > 300ms for >5m.
Permanent fixes implemented before closing: allocator heuristics patch to compact small short-lived allocations on quantized path (PR #1189); safety cap on automatic canary expansion and new rollout interlock checking latency and GPU memory metrics (PR #1194); autoscaler metric update to consider GPU memory pressure smoothed over 30s window (ENG-35500 completed); eviction policy change to introduce a 60s grace window before evicting shards that were recently accessed.
Customer communication: status updates to impacted customers posted to status.redwood.ai and targeted follow-up emails for high-usage accounts.

metrics: Observed at peak: p50 latency 45ms -> 210ms; p95 latency 220ms -> 1.2s; success rate dropped from 99.6% -> 83.4% for rerank endpoints in affected region; average GPU memory free fell by ~12% with spike in transient allocations; KV cache eviction rate increased 8x for top-10 hot shards during the canary window. Autoscaler executed 3 scale-downs followed by 4 scale-ups in 18m (oscillation).
